outlooks.summary: Severe storms are likely across portions of the Northern Plains into the Upper Midwest especially this afternoon into tonight, most likely from South Dakota and southern North Dakota into southern Minnesota, northern Iowa, and southwest Wisconsin, with a widespread damaging wind event potentially unfolding across this region.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: On the northern periphery of an upper ridge centered over the south-central Plains, an increasingly amplified belt of relatively strong mid/high-level winds will overspread the north-central CONUS.

sections.title: Northern Plains/Upper Midwest
sections.text: The possibility exists for a potentially widespread damaging wind threat to unfold across the region this afternoon especially into this evening/overnight, generally owing to a favorable location of moisture/buoyancy in relation to a seasonally strong shortwave trough and belt of westerly winds aloft. A shortwave trough and mid/upper-level speed max are readily apparent over the Pacific Northwest and northern Rockies in late-evening water vapor imagery and 00Z upper-air analysis. These features will continue to accelerate generally eastward within an increasingly fast belt of mid/high-level westerly winds aloft. As this occurs, a stalled/slow-moving frontal boundary across the north-central Plains and Upper Midwest will gradually shift northward as a warm front, with a very moist (prevalent lower 70s F surface dewpoints; 17.9 g/kg mean-mixing ratio per 00Z Omaha observed RAOB) and unstable air mass located along/south of this front. Early today, severe thunderstorms at least capable of sporadic severe hail will be possible from eastern MT into ND/northern SD this morning. sections.title: Southern/central Arizona
sections.text: Although some convective overturning has occurred across the region the prior day (Tuesday) locally stronger thunderstorms capable of severe-caliber wind gusts will be possible again this afternoon into evening.

sections.title: Southeast States
sections.text: A few strong storms capable of locally damaging winds cannot be ruled out across the region within a moist air mass, particularly across the coastal Southeast states where modestly enhanced mid-level northerly winds could support some southward-moving storm clusters. ..Guyer/Gleason.. 07/19/2017

outlooks.summary: A corridor of damaging winds, large hail, and a few tornadoes is expected to start by early afternoon near the South Dakota/North Dakota border and then spread southeastward across central/southern Minnesota through this evening, reaching southwestern Wisconsin early tonight.

sections.title: Dakotas to the Upper Midwest through this evening
sections.text: Elevated thunderstorms are developing this morning over southern ND in a zone of low-level warm advection, in advance of an embedded mid-upper speed max translating eastward from the northern Rockies. The ND storms will likely persist through the morning, though the storms could weaken later this morning while encountering diminished buoyancy per the 12z ABR sounding. Toward midday or early afternoon, lingering convection on the southern flank of the morning storms, or new development, may come into phase with the northern edge of the warm sector when the storms could become rooted at the surface. Thereafter, the storms are expected to intensify while moving southeastward across northeastern SD, central/southern MN, and eventually into parts of northeastern IA and southwestern WI/northwestern IL by tonight. A Moderate risk upgrade was considered, though lingering uncertainty regarding the details of convective evolution this afternoon precluded an upgrade in this update. A corridor of low-mid 70s boundary layer dewpoints, beneath the eastern extent of an elevated mixed layer plume, will spread northward into eastern SD and southern MN and contribute to strong buoyancy (MLCAPE of 30

sections.title: Central/southern AZ this afternoon/evening
sections.text: A weak midlevel trough over far west TX will approach southeastern AZ this evening. Clusters of storms will likely form over the Rim and mountains of southeastern AZ this afternoon, and storms will then move westward toward the lower deserts on 20 kt easterly midlevel flow. Thermodynamic profiles reflect the several previous days of convection, though there should be sufficient surface heating in cloud breaks, along with 60s boundary layer dewpoints, to support weak-moderate buoyancy and some strong downdraft potential. ..Thompson/Kerr.. 07/19/2017

outlooks.summary: Multiple corridors of damaging winds, large hail, and a few tornadoes are expected this afternoon and evening from eastern South Dakota into central/southern Minnesota, and southwestern Wisconsin.

sections.title: Dakotas into upper MS Valley
sections.text: Only minor changes have been made to the ongoing forecast. However, considerable uncertainty exists regarding the details of timing/location of the most intense severe weather later today. An MCS continues to track rapidly east-southeastward across eastern SD this morning, posing a risk of damaging winds and hail. 12z model guidance is inconsistent in the longevity of this activity, but given the proximity of the surface warm front and substantial mesoscale organization of the MCS, it appears likely it will continue through much of the day and track across southern MN into northern IA. If this scenario unfolds, a narrow corridor of enhanced wind threat could develop in that area. To the north of this convection, widespread clouds and precipitation are complicating the forecast for later today across much of south-central MN. The ongoing MCS will limit the northward return of the warm front and could short-circuit a more expansive and significant severe weather event across parts of central/southern MN this evening. However, several 12z CAMs and operational models continue to show the potential of this second scenario developing, which could include supercells and bowing structures.

sections.title: AZ
sections.text: Ample low level moisture and strong heating will once again lead to scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms over parts AZ. Gusty outflow winds will be possible in/near the stronger cells. ..Hart/Coniglio.. 07/19/2017

outlooks.summary: Several bands of damaging winds, large hail, and isolated tornadoes are expected this afternoon into tonight from eastern South Dakota into central/southern Minnesota, northern Iowa, western and southern Wisconsin into northern Illinois. Only minor changes have been made to the outlook area from the northern Plains into the upper Midwest. The primary adjustment has been to remove the far western part of the Enhanced Risk area as the initial convective system continues to progress eastward across southern Minnesota. There remains potential for a bowing QLCS to develop as this activity moves east-southeastward in close proximity to the surface warm front which extends into far northern Illinois. Large hail and damaging winds will be the primary threats with the system, with more focused swath of intense winds more likely if the system evolves into a bowing structure. There is a possibility for additional strong/severe storm development in the wake of the southern Minnesota system as a moist unstable air mass persists into central parts of South Dakota and adjacent northern Nebraska. mesoscale_discussions.summary: A mostly marginal/relatively sparse coverage severe hail/wind risk may continue across parts of south central North Dakota and north central South Dakota through 8-9 AM CDT, before convective intensities begin to wane during the mid/late morning hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Lower/mid tropospheric warm advection continues to support an area of convective development, with embedded vigorous thunderstorm activity, across parts of east central Montana into the western Dakotas. Aided by strong deep layer shear beneath 40-50 kt westerly 500 mb flow, CAPE has become sufficiently large in the presence of modestly steep mid-level lapse rates to support at least occasional marginally severe hail and gusty surface winds in the stronger storms. This may continue another couple of hours, particularly with activity spreading across parts of south central North Dakota and north central South Dakota. However, stronger supporting mid/upper forcing for ascent, downstream of the speed maximum propagating east northeast of the northern Rockies, is expected to support the continued eastward development of storms above a progressively drier and potentially cooler/stable boundary layer air mass still entrenched across the eastern Dakotas into the upper Mississippi Valley by 15-17Z. As this occurs, it seems likely that this convection will undergo appreciable weakening trends.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Potential exists for small cluster of storms over north central ND to intensify and continue through northeast SD and southwest MN with damaging wind and large hail the primary threats. However, some uncertainty remains regarding this scenario, so ww issuance will ultimately depend on convective trends.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Cluster of storms over north central ND is moving east southeast at around 35-40 kt. Based on recent observations and both model and observed 12Z RAOB data, updrafts are still elevated above a stable layer. However, sufficient dry air exists in the lowest 3 km to support strong to severe downdrafts. The storms are developing in response to a southwesterly 35 kt low-level jet that will migrate eastward with time in association with a progressive shortwave trough. These processes might help to sustain the convection until the boundary layer destabilizes sufficiently downstream to support surface based storms, and possibly a forward propagating MCS with embedded bowing segments and supercells. However, storms scale model solutions are dispersive, and some uncertainty remains whether or not storms will be able to persist as they transition to surface based given the warm elevated mixed layer with 12-14 C temperatures at 700 mb.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Some isolated severe-hail risk may accompany convection spreading across areas near and just south of the international border through the day. Present indications are that Watch issuance will be unlikely.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Regenerative convection within a corridor of modest, though capped, boundary-layer moisture return through western ND and into parts of southern Manitoba will continue to train east-southeastward. This activity will affect areas near and south of the international border through the day. Multiple, subtle foci for large-scale ascent -- accompanying a mid-level speed maximum crossing a corridor of elevated buoyancy accompanying the moisture return -- will maintain the risk for thunderstorms through the day. The 12Z Bismarck sounding indicates a layer of near 9-C/km lapse rates in the mid levels, encouraging strong upward accelerations for convection rooted atop the stable boundary layer. As potentially robust updrafts, associated with marginal to moderate elevated buoyancy, interact with 50-60 kt of effective shear -- developing eastward with time -- the most robust convective cores could produce isolated severe hail through the day. However, with effective inflow layers rooted above the stable surface layer, and given lack of more appreciable moisture return somewhat limiting buoyancy, a more substantial severe risk is not anticipated.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A small, organized cluster of thunderstorms producing severe wind gusts is expected to continue moving through the remaining portions of the Watch through 18z. A Watch will be needed soon into the MN/IA portions of the MCD area.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A cluster of thunderstorms continues moving south and east across eastern SD around 50 kt and has been producing severe wind gusts, some significant, the last few hours. Latest radar trends show indications of a mesoscale convective vortex/bookend vortex developing over western Kingsbury County that is likely contributing to the uptick in convective intensity/coverage. Although a capping inversion remains across the region, and the main lifting associated with the right-entrance region of the upper jet streak is lifting farther north away from the east-southeastward propagating system, rapid destabilization along/south of the warm front amidst low-mid 70s surface dewpoints is ongoing. Moreover, a significant cold pool is developing -- a 7-mb pressure jump was noted at KHON -- that should allow for continuation and intensification of the system in the next few hours. Given the expected movement of the current system into MN by 18z, and the potential for new convective development farther east along the warm front in IA, a Watch downstream of the current Watch is likely.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The severe wind threat is expected to continue within Watch #0420.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Although the intense southern end of the small complex of thunderstorms has decreased in intensity the last 30 minutes, continued lift will be favored to the east/east-northeast of the ongoing convection over Brookings and Moody county associated with the expanding MCV. Furthermore, continued lift along the modified warm front extending eastward into SW MN, and large, straight hodographs oriented perpendicular to the expanding cold pool edge, should maintain the system and the severe wind threat in this time period.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The risk for a few strong thunderstorms will exist into the evening hours. A couple of marginally severe storms cannot be ruled out, though Watch issuance will not be necessary.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Low-level lapse rates are steepening in response to widespread insolation from southeast and south-central AZ through central and into northwest AZ, behind scattered to widespread convective debris clouds from the lower Colorado River Valley arcing into southwest AZ. Rich deep moisture is in place across the area, with 12Z soundings at Phoenix AZ, Tucson AZ, and Las Vegas NV indicating 1.5-2.0-inch PW -- i.e., near record values per the SPC Sounding Climatology. Visible satellite images indicate increasingly agitated cumulus development over the higher terrain, with initial thunderstorm development ongoing from this activity. Thunderstorms will experience an increase in coverage and a modest increase in intensity during the next few hours, while drifting westward and northwestward into the evening hours. A slight enhancement to the mid-level flow peripheral to an MCV moving across southern AZ may support loose organization for convective structures in south-central and west-central AZ -- spreading off the Mogollon Rim to the lower deserts. Across the entire region, sufficiently steep low-level lapse rates and small-scale merging outflows may support locally strong wind gusts -- perhaps reaching marginally severe levels on a very isolated basis. Small hail may also occur over the mountains. The lack of stronger deep shear, and modest magnitude of mid-level lapse rates, will mitigate the overall severe risk.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Convection spreading toward the Atlantic Coast through the late afternoon and perhaps early evening hours may pose an isolated severe risk. Watch issuance will be unlikely.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The air mass continues to become strongly unstable ahead of an arc of loosely organized convection over the SC Piedmont. This activity will continue to spread across the coastal plain and perhaps develop into southeast GA before moving offshore -- having developed in association with a subtle lobe of mid-level ascent preceding a minor disturbance on the west side of a larger-scale trough. The Charleston SC VAD wind profile indicates around 30-40 kt of high-level northerly and north-northwesterly flow, supporting sufficient deep shear and convective ventilation for semi-organized multicell clusters to be maintained toward the Atlantic Coast. Given adequate buoyancy offered by surface temperatures having warmed into the upper 80s to lower 90s amid dewpoints in the lower/middle 70s, robust convection capable of supporting marginally severe wind/hail may occur. However, given poor mid-level lapse rates and modest deep shear, a more substantial severe risk is not expected.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A compact convective system is spreading eastward/east-southeastward across MN with accompanying severe wind/hail potential. The issuance of a Severe Thunderstorm Watch downstream of Watch 420 is forthcoming.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A compact, bowing MCS across southern MN is moving eastward to east-southeastward around 50 kt. This activity has recently attained more of a southward component to its motion, as the air mass continues to strongly destabilize near and south of a warm-frontal zone along which this system is tracking. This activity has a history of producing severe wind gusts, and will pose severe wind/hail potential as it spreads downstream of Severe Thunderstorm Watch 420. Additional details regarding the evolution of this system are contained in Mesoscale Discussion 1348, and will be contained within a forthcoming MCD.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The severe wind threat will continue within Watch #0420.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A small bowing convective system continues to move across southwestern MN at 40-45 kt. A strong MCV/northern cyclonic bookend vortex appears to have biased the overall system motion eastward the last 60-90 minutes, while the southern end of the system has not propagated into IA likely because of the northern edge of the strong capping inversion there. The rear inflow associated with the cyclonic vortex and expanding stratiform precipitation will continue to organize and expand in size the next hour or so. As the surging cold pool interacts with a very moist, unstable boundary layer observed to its east-southeast, intense convective development is expected to continue, aided by a deep-layer vertical wind shear profile very favorable for continued convective regeneration. Given the increasing influence of the rear-inflow, a general east-southeast motion is expected to resume in the next hour.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: At least isolated thunderstorm development may occur over SD near the SD-NE border. Should storms develop, a few instances of large hail and downburst winds will be possible. Given expected limited storm coverage, a WW issuance will probably not be needed unless convective trends dictate otherwise.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: As of mid afternoon a cluster of cumulus was observed increasing in vertical depth along a stalling convectively enhanced front across south central SD. This convection appears to be increasing where plume of deeply mixed hot air intersects the front and western fringe of deeper moisture. Forcing on the mesoscale is weakening with time as the progressive shortwave trough and its attendant low-level jet shifts east of this region. However, the deep mixing promoted by strong diabatic warming and frontal convergence might be sufficient to initiate isolated storms this evening. Steep lapse rates, moderate instability and 30-40 kt 0-6 km shear will support potential for updraft rotation and a threat for a few instances of large hail and downburst winds. Limiting factor for a WW issuance is expected isolated nature of the convection due to the presence of a warm elevated mixed layer and relatively weak forcing.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe threat is increasing across northeast IA, southern WI, and northern IL. Damaging winds are likely with thunderstorms this evening. WW will be issued soon to address this threat.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Long-lived MCS is beginning to turn a bit more southeast as it progresses across southeast MN and northern IA. Southern-most flank of this activity is surging southeast at roughly 50kt and will should track across the remainder of WW421, exiting the watch shortly after 23z. Damaging winds are expected along the leading edge of the squall line. WW will be issued soon to reflect this scenario.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe threat will decrease from west to east across WW421 with leading edge of squall line expected to exit the watch shortly after 20/00z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Long-lived MCS is progressing steadily southeast at 45-50kt and should exit the eastern portions of WW421 within the next hour. Damaging winds remain likely along the leading edge of the squall line and this is the primary threat as the MCS moves toward southern WI/northern IL. ..Darrow.. 07/19/2017 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Ongoing isolated large hail and damaging wind threat across WW 422 remains confined to mainly Holt County NE and vicinity in the short term.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Recent radar and visible satellite imagery shows a small thunderstorm cluster over Holt County NE which has produced isolated large hail and damaging winds over the past hour or so. A hot/moist low-level airmass persists along and south of a weak front located across northern NE into southeastern SD this evening. Steep mid-level lapse rates present on the 12Z sounding from North Platte are located across WW 422, which is contributing to strong instability (MLCAPE 2500+ J/kg). Although enhanced mid-level flow remains mostly to the north of northern NE/southern SD, veering and modest strengthening of the wind field with height is supporting around 30-40 kt of 0-6 km shear per recent VWP from KLNX. The primary thunderstorm cluster across Holt County NE has exhibited occasional supercell characteristics, and should continue to pose an isolated severe threat for the next few hours as it attempts to propagate slowly east-southeastward as a southerly low-level jet modestly strengthens this evening across central/eastern NE. Additional convection is attempting to develop farther west along the surface boundary in northern NE, and may also pose an isolated severe threat this evening. The loss of diurnal heating, increasing convective inhibition owing to a warm elevated mixed layer, and lack of large-scale upper level support all suggest the isolated severe risk should slowly diminish later this evening (generally after 02Z). ..Gleason.. 07/20/2017 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe squall line will progress across central into eastern portions of WW423 over the next two hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Long-lived MCS has cycled and matured into a fast-moving complex as it progresses across southern WI and northern IL. Latest radar data suggests the leading edge of a bow-shaped squall line is surging southeast at roughly 50kt. Given this speed/movement it appears the squall line will approach the northwestern Chicago metro between 0200-0230z, and the lake shore around 0230z. There is a possibility for widespread damaging winds along the leading edge of this convection. ..Darrow.. 07/20/2017 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Strong thunderstorms are possible across portions of northern IN and southwest lower MI. Isolated damaging winds are the primary threat.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Long-lived MCS continues its southeast movement across southern WI and northern IL. This complex of storms has cycled and matured, and now appears to be waning with warming cloud tops and weaker wind gusts along the leading squall line. Regional radar data suggests an MCV has evolved within trailing precip shield over southern WI and this feature is moving southeast toward southern Lake MI. While the MCS appears to be weakening somewhat, it remains organized and a well defined squall line is expected to progress across southern Lake MI into northern IN over the next 1-2 hours. Unless severe wind gusts become more common with an upward cycling of this complex a new ww is not anticipated.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: At least a localized severe hail to wind threat appears likely to develop southeastward across northeastern Iowa during the next several hours. Potential exists for appreciable upscale convective growth that may require a severe weather watch.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A small area of intensifying thunderstorm development, including an evolving supercell, is now ongoing near the Minnesota/Iowa Border area, in the vicinity of Fairmont MN. Mid/upper support for activity is unclear, with the primary short wave trough within the mid-latitude westerlies now passing by well to the north/northeast of the region. Activity also appears to be forming in an environment with considerable inhibition associated with elevated mixed layer area. However, lift associated with strong low-level warm advection/convergence, aided by a 30-40 kt southwesterly 850 mb jet, probably is the primary mechanism overcoming the inhibition on at least a small scale. And this may maintain ongoing activity through much of the night, with a tendency to develop southeastward across northeastern Iowa. Activity appears to be evolving to the cool side of a remnant frontal zone, but inflow of seasonably high moisture content boundary layer air from the warm sector appears to be supporting large CAPE fueling activity. Further intensification and organization of convection appears possible during the next couple of hours in the presence of seasonably strong deep layer shear. This may include a transition from a severe hail threat to an increasing damaging wind threat, with the supercell taking on a bowing structure and perhaps growing upscale.
